capabilities: Browse the LeetCode problem list with search and difficulty/status filters
Open problems as notes with locked frontmatter and a rendered problem statement
Write solutions in an embedded code editor with syntax highlighting and vim mode
Run code against sample or custom tests and submit to LeetCode's judge
Write technique wikilinks and backlinks into notes on accepted submissions
extras: AI features incur per-call provider costs (~$0.01-0.05 per accepted solution); docs include a migration path from v1.0-v1.2 with automatic backups, known limitations (vim toggle requires reload), and a troubleshooting section.
motivation: The README says solved problems should become 'tagged, linked, and discoverable' notes so practice builds a knowledge graph instead of scattered code files.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to fetch coding problems, edit solutions with a real code editor, or submit them to LeetCode's judge, so practice ends up as scattered code files.

relations.evidence: This plugin communicates with leetcode.com to fetch problems and submit solutions.
only when you have configured an active AI provider in Settings → AI
relations.plugin: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, AWS Bedrock

summary: LeetCode integration that lets you browse problems, solve them in an embedded code editor, and run or submit solutions from inside your vault.
